prompt: Write StrictThermostat, a subclass that narrows what its parent accepts by overriding one protected hook -- and prove it holds even through a Thermostat reference. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: The parent keeps target private and setTarget final, so the single point of extension is the protected allows hook; overriding it narrows the accepted values without the subclass ever touching the field. Calling super.allows(value) first means the subclass adds to the parent's rule rather than replacing it. Because Java always dispatches to the override, a StrictThermostat held in a Thermostat variable still refuses 36 -- the stricter invariant travels with the object, not with the reference type.
hints: The override should read super.allows(value) && ... so the parent's range check still applies.
value % 2 == 0 is the even test; combine it with the 15..25 bounds.
In the constructor the parent may already have stored a value this class rejects, so call setTarget(value) and fall back to setTarget(18) when it returns false.
